How to read the plots and robustness score

The modeled line is the original GPT-assignment GAM trend. Counts and denominators enter the models, including years with zero hits. A frame occurrence means one classified text assigned that frame; repeated mentions within that text are not counted separately. Raw frequency shows the actual yearly GPT hits, with no GAM, normalization or uncertainty ribbon.

The ribbon shows how far the estimated level could move under the assumptions we tested. For each scenario we simulate 2,000 whole curves. At each year, we take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of those values—the middle 95%. The ribbon runs from the lowest lower bound to the highest upper bound across scenarios, and also contains the displayed line. It is not the middle 95% of a pooled set of simulations, or a 95% guarantee that the true curve lies inside it.

A wide ribbon means different coding or model assumptions allow substantially different frame frequencies. It does not mean every line inside it is equally plausible, or that one simulated curve follows either edge. Level and direction are different: scenarios can shift a curve up or down while agreeing that it rises. The comparisons include GAM uncertainty, smoother flexibility, bounded temporal correlation, and alternative annotation references. Four frames have their own audits; the other frames borrow their error scenarios as stress tests, which can make their ribbons particularly wide.

Robustness measures direction, not size or importance. Grey means weaker agreement; blue and purple mean stronger agreement across the tested scenarios. In each scenario we count how many simulated slopes point in the same direction as the displayed GAM. We take the lowest agreement across scenarios and calculate max(0, 2 × agreement − 1). Before colour averaging, a score of 0.90 means 95% directional agreement, and 0.95 means 97.5%. No minimum effect size was imposed, so a small but consistently positive slope can score highly.

Line colour shows a five-year mean of that score. The 0.90 marker is a descriptive high-agreement guide, not a significance cutoff, proof of a real change, or a measure of substantive importance. The tooltip separately gives the actual yearly agreement in the least supportive scenario. Endpoints and excluded support years can have a zero score.

Uniform gives every visible panel the same y-axis maximum, recomputed from the current country/trait filters and visible marks. Frame-variable shares a scale between Congress and Hansard for each frame. Every axis starts at zero. Consider the axis and amount of change alongside robustness.
